meta.title: Northstar Growth Fund III PME (TEST)
meta.subtitle: Commitment cash-flow evidence versus public markets

evidence.unavailable_reason: The sensitivity benchmark did not have governed returns for the commitment cash-flow window.

limitations: The primary benchmark produced usable PME evidence, but the separately requested sensitivity benchmark was unavailable.
Holdings and ILPA company detail are contextual and were not used as PME calculator inputs.

selection.rationale: PME evidence informs investment diligence but does not determine a manager-selection decision.

executive.bottom_line: Northstar Growth Fund III (TEST) returned 1.08x KS-PME and 12.6% IRR against the primary benchmark through 2025-12-31, while the separate sensitivity path remained unavailable [S6][S7].

sections.title: Executive conclusion
sections.kicker: Primary PME is positive but the alternate benchmark path is unresolved

blocks.title: Key judgment — Primary result
blocks.text: Observation: The primary server run returned 1.08x KS-PME through 2025-12-31 [S6]. Why it matters: The fund exceeded the selected public-market equivalent on the returned cash-flow basis. Uncertainty: Direct alpha was not returned by the server. What would change the view: A refreshed primary run at or below 1.00x KS-PME.

blocks.title: Key judgment — Benchmark sensitivity
blocks.text: Observation: One of two separately requested benchmark sessions was usable [S5][S7]. Why it matters: Relative performance has not been tested against the alternate basis. Uncertainty: The missing path could materially change interpretation. What would change the view: A sensitivity session returning KS-PME below 1.00x.

blocks.title: Key judgment — Cash-flow context
blocks.text: Observation: The PME run returned 12.6% IRR and 1.41x TVPI, with 0.66x distributed and 0.75x residual value [S6]. Why it matters: More value remains unrealized than distributed. Uncertainty: Holdings context is not a calculator input. What would change the view: Audited cash flows changing TVPI by at least 0.10x.

blocks.title: Analysis — Primary PME result
blocks.text: Observation: The returned KS-PME was 1.08x against the primary benchmark through 2025-12-31 [S6]. Why it matters: The observed cash-flow path modestly exceeded the public-market equivalent. Uncertainty: Direct alpha was null and the sensitivity run was unavailable. What would change the view: A complete alternate-benchmark result below 1.00x.

blocks.title: Analysis — Realized and residual value
blocks.text: Observation: The tool returned 12.6% IRR, 1.41x TVPI, 0.66x DPI, and 0.75x RVPI [S6]. Why it matters: Residual value slightly exceeds distributed value. Uncertainty: ILPA coverage is incomplete for three of 18 holdings [S3]. What would change the view: Audited cash flows shifting DPI or RVPI by at least 0.10x.

blocks.title: Analysis — Sensitivity gap
blocks.text: Observation: The primary path returned 1.08x KS-PME, while the distinct sensitivity builder returned no session [S6][S7]. Why it matters: Benchmark dependence remains unresolved across the two selected public-market bases. Uncertainty: Sensitivity coverage is limited because no alternate PME value supports a range. What would change the view: A separately built sensitivity session returning KS-PME at or below 1.00x.

blocks.title: Governed evidence boundary
blocks.text: The primary and sensitivity requests use the same canonical portfolio and commitment IDs but distinct benchmark IDs and separately built sessions [S5][S7]. Only the primary session produced server-computed PME evidence [S6]. Holdings and ILPA context remain a separate source lane and are never calculator inputs [S3].

blocks.title: Decision-use boundary
blocks.text: This partial report is supported because one benchmark path returned usable PME evidence [S6]. The unavailable sensitivity path stays reader-visible with its typed error and request ID [S7]. If both paths had returned zero usable analytical evidence, the skill contract would require a chat-only unavailable response rather than a report.
